name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in still frames without creating halos or artifacts, which directly boosts visual clarity—even a 0.5% gain in perceived sharpness matters for high-stakes outputs. The trade-off is compute cost: it adds ~15% runtime per frame, but only on the final upscale step, so the net impact on throughput is small.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal problem, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting 15% compute on a dead end while the blur persists. Test VFI-Flow’s 20% throughput drop against a motion-compensated upscaler like FILM or XVFI++—if either cuts blur without tanking speed, that’s the play.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames by estimating per-pixel motion vectors, which directly attacks the core problem of temporal smearing—no other tool in the stack does this. The trade-off is a 20% drop in throughput, but blur reduction compounds with every frame, making the net quality gain worth the slower output for high-stakes scenes.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 20% throughput hit isn’t a trade-off—it’s a pipeline breaker on low-latency outputs. A better alternative: test FILM or XVFI++ first; if either cuts blur without tanking speed, default to it. Settle it with a side-by-side run: same input, measure blur reduction vs. throughput—no guesswork.
